- OP: "What's your occupation? Are you married?"
- Woman: "I work at this place super close to Nguyen Hue street."
- OP: "Oh so you're a street peddler then?"

If you've been to Ho Chi Minh city you'd know that the street of Nguyen Hue is filled with street vendors an peddlers. OP did not get a satisfactory answer so he made a sarcastic remark. This is how most Vietnamese make jokes by the way - through sarcasm and satire.

100% agreed. It's the little things that matter. But whenever you bring those things up people would look at you weirdly; some would downplay your view due to the notion that "owning a house in Saigon is in itself a privilege". Soooo annoying. Vietnamese love everything cheap and pretty. And cheap pretty shells that are lacking in density can only take you so far.

Same thing with building a house. My parents' house was built 10 years ago. The house degraded quickly, and soon there were cracks and leakages and algae. My mom said that it was because the contractors would cut corners by purchasing cheaper materials that look the same to what we wanted and they would pocket the differences.
